lead: Tesla / TSLA — the loyalty meets the registration data
smaller: Hims & Hers / HIMS — the weight-loss trade with a 2X fund
Archer Aviation / ACHR — the meme stock with a Palantir deal
why_lead: Quantum is out as the lead. The 13 March lead and the 14 March D-Wave smaller trade already told the breakthrough and the IonQ issuance stories, and D-Wave's 14 March session (+46.89%) changes the price but not the story. Tesla is the best-supported distinct story today: a 29.77% drawdown over 20 sessions that retail holders are still defending, and the new evidence is all dated 13 to 16 March (JPMorgan and CNBC on 13 March, The Verge's registrations headline on 14 March, Fortune's Robinhood holdings ranking on 14 March, Cathie Wood and Business Insider on 15 March, Business Insider's retail holders piece on 16 March). It is a changed story from the 12 March lead: that essay called the drop a political storm and named a weak demand print as the break, and falling registrations are that print.
why_smaller: Gold is the non-equity trade and its evidence is unchanged from the draft: gold futures at 3,001.10 sit on the $3,000 headline, with Bloomberg and Reuters on 14 March and MarketWatch on 15 March, and the Wednesday Fed decision is the pending event. No earlier edition traded gold; the 7 March silver essay mentioned gold only as a hook.

Hims & Hers replaces the NuScale trade. HIMS is down 44.00% over 20 sessions, Defiance launched the HIMZ 2X ETF on 12 March, and the 13 and 14 March headlines tie the fall in weight-loss stocks to the semaglutide market. NuScale's Amazon, Google and nuclear-pledge evidence had already been used in the 11 March Oklo smaller trade and the 13 March nuclear trade.

Archer replaces the earlier Tesla smaller trade, whose loyalty angle has moved into the lead. Archer is the air-taxi trade with a dated Palantir partnership (13 and 14 March), the meme-stock label (13 March) and an 8.97% session on 14 March; Joby's 16 March Stocktwits chatter is cited as sector context only.
considered_not_chosen: Quantum (D-Wave, Rigetti, IonQ): the largest move on 14 March (QBTS up 46.89% and RGTI up 28.23% in the session), but the story repeats the 13 March lead and the 14 March D-Wave smaller trade (the breakthrough and the IonQ raise); the Rigetti placement is a new fact, not enough for a fourth quantum essay in ten days.
Robinhood (HOOD): the 11 March lead already covered the crash from 55.86 to 35.63; the 14 March bounce to 39.24 and the 15 March 'bull trap' idea are price and chart evidence, not a new story.
NuScale and nuclear: the Amazon and Google pledge (CNBC, 12 March) and the Oklo and NuScale smaller trades of 4, 11 and 13 March already cover this story.
Nvidia (NVDA): retail's No. 1 held stock on Robinhood (Fortune, 14 March) is used as evidence in the Tesla lead rather than as a trade; the moves are modest (+5.27% in the session, -10.07% over 20).

SoFi (SOFI): a $5 billion Blue Owl loan agreement and a 'best meme stock' listicle on 13 March, with a 20.41% drawdown, but no surge; it was weaker than Hims on the drawdown and the leveraged-product signal.
Bitcoin (BTC): Cathie Wood's $80 million Bitcoin buy as BTC fell below $83K (14 March) is a dated flow, but Bitcoin was a smaller trade on 6 and 10 March.
Rocket Lab (RKLB): a 2X ETF, a planned $500 million equity raise and a spacecraft deployment, but the name was already a smaller trade on 11 March.
Sandisk (SNDK): +52.28% over 20 sessions, but the new items are a product launch and a product review; the 10 March smaller trade already covered the relisting.

Joby Aviation (JOBY): the 16 March Stocktwits chatter is a clean attention item, but the card move (+4.17% in the session, -17.68% over 20) is weaker than Archer's; Joby is cited as sector context in the Archer trade.
Intel, Dogecoin, Rheinmetall, Palantir, Silver: each repeats an earlier lead or smaller angle with no new catalyst in the feed.
